understanding: The supplied source confirms the local F5 behavior: FileSnapshotSink.Close and Cancel set closed before finalization, and subsequent calls return nil without retrying or checking the earlier outcome (file_snapshot.go:397:498). This establishes lifecycle entry, not publication. takeSnapshot runs on the snapshot thread, calls Persist, aborts and invokes Cancel when Persist returns an error, and otherwise checks Close before advancing snapshot metadata and requesting bounded log compaction (snapshot.go:125:278). Thus propagation of the original failure through Persist prevents the hypothesized compaction path. FSMSnapshot.Persist instructs applications to write all necessary state and call Close when finished or Cancel on error; the supplied interface comments do not explicitly specify propagation of Close errors or retry semantics (fsm.go:1:81; snapshot.go:1:124). That omission does not establish that suppressing an error is contract-compliant. The remaining discriminator is whether an applicable caller can legally return nil after unsuccessful finalization or cancellation. No defect, usable replacement snapshot, or loss of recoverability is established. F5's existing meaning should remain unchanged; any eventual publication fact must distinguish initial successful finalization from the already-closed branch.
